zones.label: Resistor Bands
zones.summary: Colored bands encode resistance, multiplier, tolerance, and sometimes temperature coefficient.
facts: Read directly: Nominal resistance and tolerance using the resistor color code.
Physical clue: A separated tolerance band helps establish reading direction.
Look up or calculate: Power rating is estimated from package size and confirmed by the part specification.

zones.label: Diode Stripe
zones.summary: The body stripe identifies the cathode and therefore the diode's orientation.
facts: Read directly: The stripe marks the cathode on most axial diodes.
Physical clue: LED packages may use a flat edge and lead length instead of a printed stripe.
Look up: Forward voltage, maximum current, and reverse-voltage rating.

zones.label: Transistor Face
zones.summary: The printed part number identifies the device; the flat face is only an orientation reference.
facts: Read directly: A printed code or part number, when present.
Physical clue: The flat face helps describe orientation but does not guarantee a universal E-B-C pin order.
Look up: Exact pinout, polarity, package, current, voltage, gain, and power limits.

zones.label: Capacitor Marks
zones.summary: Printed value, voltage, and polarity marks reveal essential installation information.
facts: Read directly: Capacitance code or value, working voltage, and polarity when marked.
Physical clue: On common aluminum electrolytics, the stripe usually marks the negative terminal.
Look up: Dielectric type, tolerance, temperature range, and ripple-current rating.

zones.label: IC Notch & Dot
zones.summary: A notch or dot establishes pin-numbering orientation; the part code identifies function.
facts: Read directly: Part number, manufacturer code, and sometimes date or lot code.
Physical clue: The notch or dot locates pin 1 so pins can be counted correctly.
Look up: Pin functions, supply range, truth table, timing, and absolute maximum ratings.

quiz.question: Which marking system encodes a numerical value using colored bands?
quiz.explanation: Resistor bands encode significant digits, multiplier, and tolerance.

quiz.question: Which visible mark normally identifies a cathode?
quiz.explanation: The stripe on an axial diode marks its cathode.

quiz.question: Which flat-faced package still requires a datasheet because its three leads have no universal order?
quiz.explanation: The transistor part number and datasheet determine the pinout.

quiz.question: Which component commonly prints both capacitance and a working-voltage rating?
quiz.explanation: Capacitors commonly show capacitance, voltage, and polarity information.

quiz.question: Which component uses a notch or dot to establish where pin numbering begins?
quiz.explanation: IC notches and dots provide pin-1 orientation.
